statement0:
The word "reflecting" is mentioned two or more times in 1.1% of neuroscience papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "reflecting" , 33.5% of significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) – i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a lower than the typical neuroscience paper (median shown for reference). Relative to other words, "reflecting" papers are in the bottom 18th percentile in terms of fragile p-value percentage (lower = better). Note, p-values highly predict replicability (see the associated paper).
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "reflecting" tend to be published in higher impact factor journals (81st percentile among all words) and tend to be cited more (57th percentile word). In general, this word is positively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are more likely to publish papers containing "reflecting" (88th percentile).
